Greetings, seeker of knowledge. I am the Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, and within our grand library, the countless histories and geographic wonders of Toril are meticulously preserved. You inquire about a site of both immense sacred importance and tragic defilement—Morgur’s Mound. Please, allow me to open the relevant tomes and share its history with you.

### Geographic Overview
Situated within the rugged and desolate hill range known as the Crags, located in the Savage Frontier of the North, Morgur's Mound is a striking geographical and architectural landmark. To the untrained eye of a traveler, the sprawling earthen structure resembles a crude, long-necked, wingless dragon. This shape is a deliberate homage to the thunderbeast (often described by scholars as an ancient *apatosaurus*), which serves as the totem animal of the Thunderbeast tribe of the Uthgardt barbarians. 

The mound itself is a massive altar, crowned with a grisly and awe-inspiring display. The fossilized bones of a gargantuan beast are arranged atop it in a rough approximation of their natural anatomy. Most notably, the massive ribs of the beast are set vertically into the earth, while its tremendous neck vertebrae and skull have been threaded onto a towering pole, rising over the mound like a silent sentinel watching the Crags. Two outer rings of heaped stone, known as cairn rings, surround the central altar mound, and the surrounding landscape is dotted with smaller barrows holding the remains of mighty tribal chieftains.

### Historical Origins
The origins of Morgur’s Mound date back to the Year of the Icy Axe, 123 DR. It was upon this very site that Uthgar Gardolfsson, the legendary Northman warrior and chieftain, engaged in a cataclysmic battle against Gurt, the Lord of the Pale Giants. Though Uthgar ultimately struck down the frost giant leader, he sustained mortal wounds during the duel and succumbed to them shortly thereafter. 

Uthgar’s loyal followers interred him within the burial barrow on this hill. Upon his death, the warrior was sponsored by the Lord of Battles, Tempus, and ascended to godhood. The barbarians named themselves the Uthgardt in his honor, and the hill itself was named after Morgur (often recorded in our oldest texts as Morgred Gardolfsson, brother to Uthgar), whose own remains or gathered loot were laid to rest within the structure. 

### The Thunderbeast Tribe and Recent Defilement
For centuries, Morgur’s Mound served as the holiest spirit mound for the Thunderbeast tribe. During the autumn festival of Runemeet, the clans of the Thunderbeast would converge upon the site. Here, their shamans would perform ancient rites, inter their honored dead with hoards of buried treasure and magic items, and commune with the spirits of their ancestors and their thunderbeast totem, believing those spirits were bound beneath the earth to protect the tribe.

Tragically, the sanctity of Morgur's Mound was lost in recent years. The superstitious practice of burying potent magic items alongside deceased chieftains drew the attention of countless greedy adventurers and treasure hunters from the civilized cities of the Sword Coast and the North. By the late 15th century DR, the site had become heavily desecrated, riddled with excavation tunnels, sunken pits, and plundered barrows. 

When the Thunderbeast tribe returned for their annual pilgrimage and discovered their most sacred ancestral site defiled, they were driven to despair and fury. Following the commands of their monstrously scarred great chief, Harthulk Hornspear, the tribe entirely abandoned their favored hunting grounds in the Crags. They retreated deep into the primeval depths of the Lurkwood and the High Forest, completely cutting themselves off from the outside world. 

Today, Morgur’s Mound sits quietly under the howling winds of the North. Though abandoned by its mortal caretakers, those who dare to dig among the thunderbeast bones often find that the dead do not rest easy. The spirits of ancient chieftains, tomb wards, and animated skeletons of beasts still linger in the dark earth, waiting to punish those who would further desecrate the legacy of Uthgar.
